title: Read an Analog Input
description: Read a varying voltage from a potentiometer using analogRead(), and print it to the Serial Monitor.

steps.clip: Grab an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, a 10 kΩ potentiometer (a turning knob) and three jumper wires.
Push the knob into the breadboard so each of its three legs is in a different numbered column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
Two legs in the same column would be connected to each other, so use three different columns.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Take a jumper wire from one of the outer legs' columns to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Either outer leg works — swapping them only makes the reading go the other way when you turn the knob.
Any GND pin on the Arduino works.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the knob to GND.

steps.clip: Take a wire from the other outer leg's column to the 5V pin on the Arduino.
hints: It's the outer leg you haven't wired yet.
steps.goal: Connect the other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Take the last wire from the middle leg's column to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: The middle leg's voltage changes as you turn the knob; pin A0 measures it.
Pin A0 is on the Arduino's bottom-right row of sockets, marked ANALOG IN.
steps.goal: Connect the middle leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Upload the code, then open the Serial Monitor. You'll see a number from 0 to 1023 that changes as you turn the knob.
